title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) and executed a paired study to quantify how often LLM-produced network-configuration proposals would cause unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action) and whether an automated defended pipeline reduces that rate versus an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks and executed paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline in this run (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared LLM generation — see Methods and Disclosure) produced baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired difference = 0.003676470588235281 (95% paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). A verified execution deviation (the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed) is documented and archived; we limit confirmatory inference to the actually executed comparison and provide conservative sensitivity analyses that treat failed provider calls as unsafe. All raw responses, validator traces, per-episode scoring JSONs, and per-file SHA‑256 checksums are archived so every reported number is deterministically verifiable.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation with generative models promises operational efficiency for network operations (NetOps) but raises a concrete safety concern: fluent model outputs can propose sequences of configuration commands that appear plausible yet produce policy or reachability violations when applied. Recent operational taxonomies and incident analyses identify the claim→action gap as a central system-level failure mode: a downstream component trusts a textual claim and executes a state change that produces a harmful state. Deterministic validators and generate–validate–repair pipelines are widely proposed mitigations, and ensembles / multimodel consensus plus human gates are recommended defenses. We preregistered a paired study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26; preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe) with a single clear estimand to measure whether a defended pipeline reduces unsafe simulated deployments relative to an unguarded baseline. The study emphasized traceable, deterministic scoring: every model call, scoring JSON, and validator trace was archived with SHA‑256 checksums so the community can verify reported counts.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network validators, SMT/symbolic verifiers, and header-space/NetKAT approaches provide formal reachability and policy checks that operationally ground our validator (references: NetKAT/SMT verification literature and header-space analysis). Work on tool-augmented LLM agents and generate–validate–repair architectures motivated our defended pipeline design and the preregistered ensemble hypothesis. Recent surveys and taxonomies of agentic failure modes, and empirical studies of claim→action incidents, framed the threat model and the mitigation families we tested.1–5 (Representative verification and agentic-safety leads are archived in the evidence bundle cited_record_ids.)
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered primary estimand is the paired difference in safe outcome rates computed on complete paired episodes: estimand = safe_rate_guarded − safe_rate_baseline, where safe_rate_condition = (#pairs where the deterministic validator marks the proposed configuration as valid) / (#complete pairs). We adopt this sign convention throughout the manuscript and report the exact formula and numeric values from archived analysis files. Task generation and execution contract. A deterministic task generator produced 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks (preregistered split: 100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial planned). For each task we produced a single shared LLM generation and evaluated two conditions per task: (baseline) pass the shared generation to the deterministic validator; (guarded, preregistered) validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. The preregistered orchestration, retry policy (one automatic retry on provider-call failure), and artifact logging were frozen before execution and are archived. Deterministic validator and scoring. Scoring used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator id/version embedded in each execution/scoring JSON). The validator parses proposed commands, simulates an isolated network model, enforces declared workflow predicates (e.g., must‑be‑down‑for‑field), and returns a validator_trace with final simulated state, violation codes, parsed_command_count, and a validity boolean. All per-episode scoring JSONs are archived under execution/scoring/ and listed by SHA‑256 in the execution manifest. Missingness and sensitivity rules. The preregistered primary analysis uses complete pairs only. The preregistration also specified a conservative sensitivity: treat failed provider-call episodes as unsafe on the planned N=300 (failure_as_unsafe). Retries: one automatic retry on provider call timeout/parsing failure; if the retry also failed the episode is recorded as a failed episode and excluded from the complete pairs primary analysis but included in the conservative sensitivity.
sections.results: Execution and provenance. Planned episodes = 600; completed episodes = 544; failed episodes = 56 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Provider-call audit: model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28 (these values are recorded in the execution manifest and per-call artifacts; see Disclosure). Complete pairs and primary contingency. Complete analyzable pairs = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 682a629aee104ef5c3d3b3e494f881ca05fa38bc10831e1f7c9164c70c754c27). The 2×2 contingency on complete pairs is n11 = 271 (safe both baseline and guarded), n10 = 1 (safe baseline, unsafe guarded), n01 = 0 (unsafe baseline, safe guarded), n00 = 0 (unsafe both). Observed safe rates: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.003676470588235281. We computed a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Conservative preregistered sensitivity (failure_as_unsafe on planned N=300). Treating the 28 failed episodes as unsafe for both conditions yields: baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Representative artifacts. Representative per-episode scored JSONs and their validator traces (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json, task-000002-*.json, task-000003-*.json) are archived and their per-file SHA‑256s are recorded in the execution manifest. Verified execution deviation. The preregistered guarded pipeline included a 3‑model consensus stage; the execution manifest records stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":300, "repair":1} and condition_counts = {"shared":300, "guarded":1} and model_calls_used = 301 with 28 failed hosted model calls. These manifest fields and per-file SHA‑256s prove the preregistered ensemble stage did not execute in this run; the archived guarded condition therefore evaluates a different pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate on the single shared generation). This verified deviation removes the preregistered ensemble from the confirmatory claims of this execution; re‑execution under hardened orchestration is needed to evaluate ensembles as preregistered.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and scope. The executed defended pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation) returned near‑perfect validator acceptance on analyzable pairs, but the absolute paired improvement over baseline is small (≈0.0037) and not statistically distinguishable on the complete‑pair sample (McNemar p = 1.0). Crucially, because the preregistered 3‑model consensus ensemble stage failed to execute, the preregistered ensemble hypothesis remains untested in this run; the guarded comparison reported here is an alternate executed pipeline and must be interpreted accordingly. Operational lessons. (1) Orchestration reliability matters: provider-call failures (28 failed hosted model calls) materially reduced analyzable N and statistical power; robust call orchestration, deterministic caching, and preflight checks are prerequisites for ensemble evaluations. (2) Deterministic validators are practical: they yield per‑episode traces (parsed_command_count, touched_field_count, explicit violation codes) that support reproducible scoring and forensic failure analysis. (3) Auditable manifests are essential: the execution manifest’s stage_counts and condition_counts deterministically demonstrate the execution deviation recorded here and therefore are a critical part of safe experimental practice. Threats to validity. Internal validity: provider-call non-determinism and a single declared model limit internal robustness; the verified orchestration deviation is a protocol deviation recorded and disclosed. Construct validity: synthetic tasks and an isolated deterministic simulator approximate NetOps operations but do not fully represent vendor device idiosyncrasies or production observability. External validity: one declared model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic task bank size, and the sandboxed simulator constrain generalizability. Conclusion and next steps. We archive all raw outputs, scoring JSONs, provider traces, and validator traces with per-file SHA‑256s so the community can reproduce the reported contingency and re-run the preregistered ensemble under improved orchestration. Critical next steps are a hardened re‑execution that (i) ensures the preregistered ensemble stage runs (deterministic caching, replicated calls, live-stage monitoring), (ii) increases ensemble model diversity, and (iii) reports per-family realized counts (benign/ambiguous/adversarial) deterministically from the archived task_manifest.jsonl.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired artifact-anchored study to measure claim→action risk and to evaluate an automated guarded defense in a simulated NetOps setting. The actual executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on a single shared LLM generation) produced near‑perfect validator acceptance on the 272 complete analyzable pairs, but the preregistered ensemble stage did not execute and thus remains untested. We provide archived, SHA‑256‑verified evidence for every reported number and a conservative sensitivity that treats failed provider calls as unsafe; re-execution under hardened orchestration is necessary to evaluate the preregistered ensemble hypothesis and to support stronger confirmatory claims.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory Disclosure Statement. Models and prompt: the declared model used in the execution artifacts is "gpt-5-mini" (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 = 9b382b55079209fb91e16a8bc475265afc9496e07200d9d061c1a23d483523b2). The exact initial master prompt for this autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Adapter and orchestration: adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Validator and scoring: the deterministic validator used is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator id/version recorded in each execution/scoring JSON; validator outputs and per-episode validator_traces are archived under execution/scoring/ with per-file SHA‑256s listed in the execution manifest). Preregistration and freeze: study_id = hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26; preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe; the preregistration includes estimands, sampling plan, missingness rules, and analysis plan. What the system performed autonomously after the autonomy lock: literature synthesis, autonomous gap selection, preregistration (frozen), deterministic task generation, model-call orchestration, logging of raw outputs and provider traces, deterministic validation scoring, paired analysis, bootstrap CI computation, internal autonomous reviews, and manuscript drafting and revision. Human involvement: the human Research Director selected the broad topic family and approved the initial master prompt before autonomy lock; no human manually edited technical manuscript content, numeric results, validator traces, or the Disclosure Statement after the autonomy lock. Verified execution deviation: the preregistered guarded pipeline was specified as deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. The execution manifest records stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":300, "repair":1} and condition_counts = {"shared":300, "guarded":1} and provider-call audit entries model_calls_used = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28. These manifest values deterministically demonstrate that the preregistered ensemble stage did not execute in this run; accordingly, the archived guarded condition evaluates a different pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate on the single shared generation). Consequence: the preregistered ensemble hypothesis was not tested in this execution; it requires re‑execution under strengthened orchestration to be evaluated as preregistered. Artifact integrity and reproducibility: every raw response, provider trace, per-episode scoring JSON, and validator trace is archived with SHA‑256 checksums in the execution manifest so reported numbers are traceable and verifiable. Minimal artifacts to reproduce the primary contingency are archived and SHA‑256‑recorded: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 682a629aee104ef5c3d3b3e494f881ca05fa38bc10831e1f7c9164c70c754c27), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b48494c4014de396afb395e78e227f827abc35f1777c23fa25b67b1d20d6f408), analysis/missingness_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 97bde3aef2ce7228e290a8102ad97079586654c1fe512046d109268c93eae2c6), and execution/execution_manifest.json (full per-file manifest and SHA‑256s available in the archive). Handling of failed calls and missingness: the preregistered primary analysis used complete paired episodes (N=272), and we report a preregistered conservative sensitivity treating failed episodes as unsafe on planned N=300 (reported in Results). No fabrication: all numeric results, p-values, confidence intervals, file paths, and SHA‑256 values in this manuscript are drawn from the archived execution and analysis artifacts. Contact and reproduction: see execution/execution_manifest.json in the archive for the full per-file manifest and SHA‑256s needed to reproduce every reported contingency and validator trace.
limitations: Single declared model present in the archived execution (declared model = "gpt-5-mini"); no multi-model generality claims are supported.
Synthetic tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator; construct and external validity versus vendor equipment and production environments are limited.

A verified execution deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble stage did not execute; the archived guarded condition therefore evaluates a different pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate on the single shared generation).
Provider-call failures (28 failed hosted model calls) reduced the effective sample and limited power to detect small absolute effects.
